definition: Jurisprudence means the philosophy and science of law — and, concretely, the accumulated body of court decisions and principles a legal system reasons from.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word jurisprudence. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know jurisprudence should be able to work it out from your sentence.

At her retirement dinner, Judge Arroyo was praised less for any single decision than for her command of the nation's jurisprudence.
Colleagues described how she could trace a question backward through eighty years of decisions, then forward through the principles those decisions had slowly built.
Young lawyers remembered her chambers exams: name the holding, then explain the reasoning a court would use to extend it.
The law, she liked to say, was not a rulebook but a long conversation.
What she carried in her head was the whole conversation at once — every major decision, and the philosophy threaded through them.
